papers.title_en: Deep Thought Alignment: Trajectory-Level Latent Distillation for Video Reasoning
papers.authors: Ao Shen, Yongheng Zhang, Yinghui Li, Manning Wang, Di Yin, Xing Sun
papers.evidence: 提出Latent-OPD，一种同时约束潜在表示的on-policy蒸馏变体
papers.tldr: 视频推理大模型因处理海量视觉信息而计算成本高昂，促使研究者将大模型推理能力蒸馏到更小的模型。现有On-Policy Distillation (OPD)通过匹配学生生成轨迹上的输出token分布进行迁移，但视频推理常需跨帧累积证据，输出级监督仅捕捉表达出的信息，未直接约束推理过程形成的潜在表示。为此，我们提出Latent-OPD，在OPD基础上增加轨迹级潜在蒸馏，聚焦每条轨迹末尾的隐藏状态以总结视觉证据与推理上下文；同时提出渐进式teacher-lookahead策略，将学生中后层与教师越来越深的层对齐。在六个视频推理基准上的实验表明，Latent-OPD一致优于仅输出级OPD，尤其在帧数有限、长视频或需要复杂证据聚合的任务中提升显著，最终确立了其在帧高效视频推理中的高效性。
papers.abstract_en: Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) for video reasoning have long been hindered by the high computational cost of processing vast amounts of visual information. This dilemma motivates the transfer of the reasoning capabilities of large models to smaller, more efficient ones. On-Policy Distillation (OPD) offers a promising solution by matching output-token distributions along student-generated trajectories. However, video reasoning often depends on evidence accumulated across multiple frames. In this context, output-level supervision only captures information expressed through token predictions and does not directly constrain the latent representations formed during reasoning. To address this limitation, we propose Latent-OPD, which augments OPD with trajectory-level latent distillation. Specifically, our method focuses on the position at the end of each trajectory, where hidden states effectively summarize the accumulated visual evidence and reasoning context. Furthermore, we introduce a progressive teacher-lookahead strategy, which aligns middle-to-late student layers with increasingly deeper teacher layers. Experiments on six video reasoning benchmarks show that Latent-OPD consistently outperforms output-only OPD. Notably, the improvements are particularly pronounced in scenarios with limited frames, long videos, or tasks requiring complex evidence aggregation. These results establish Latent-OPD as a highly effective approach to frame-efficient video reasoning.
